title: Coroner's inquest called into Andrew Loku's death in police shooting
article: A Coroner's inquest has been called into the police shooting death of Andrew Loku.

In March, the Special Investigations Unit determined that an officer used "justifiable force" when he fatally shot the 45-year-old in July 2015. The SIU investigation found that two officers encountered Loku in a third floor hallway of an apartment at 502 Gilbert Avenue around midnight on July 5, 2015. He was armed with a hammer.
"Both responding officers repeatedly directed Mr. Loku to drop the hammer and they gave him ample opportunity to do so," SIU Director Tony Loparco said in a released statement.
Loku's death and the absolving of police wrongdoing has fueled Black Lives Matter protests in Toronto.

Activists camped out in front of Toronto police headquarters for two weeks, demanding a provincial review of the SIU. They also wanted the names of officers involved in Loku's shooting to be released.
Protesters also held a vigil for Loku in front of Premier Kathleen Wynne's home, sparking a police investigation.
The Coroner's inquest will examine the events surrounding Loku's death and a jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths, the coroner's office said in a release.
